analysis.title: GS MORNING (Slater, 12 Nov 2026)
key_insights: October CPI printed 30bps (0.3% m/m) even though noisy categories (airfares, health insurance, car prices) printed to the downside. GS US Economics (Walker) says this makes it harder to hold the view that inflation is transitory. Near-term inflation forecasts should move somewhat higher, 'not a sea change' but 'a hotter direction'.

GS EM FX Trading (Mediratta) likes long CNH, funded with a basket of EUR and SGD. October trade surplus above $100bn has driven RMB appreciation. A 2% hike in the foreign currency deposit RRR, followed by a one-off higher onshore fixing, was symbolic and aimed at slowing appreciation, not reversing it.

GS expects gradual RMB appreciation to continue with top leadership backing, since it keeps trade tension muted with the US and Europe. A re-entry into long CNH is flagged once the spot-fixing gap is near -200/-300 pips, targeting faster-than-carry appreciation into January on seasonal exporter repatriation.

GS FX Strategy (Jenkins): energy prices have fallen sharply month-to-date and the Energy FX factor is down about 2.2% in November. FX reacts more to oil-higher days than oil-lower days. Brent is just under midway through its energy shock range, TTF is closer to its highs.

NOKSEK has held more of its gains, consistent with stickier energy passthrough, and remains one of the FX pairs most levered to energy. AUDNZD is further off its highs, with domestic factors playing a bigger role. The trade-weighted USD made new YTD highs on 11 Nov despite lower energy prices.

GS US Economics (Rindels): real business fixed investment grew at an 11% annualized rate in 2026Q1-Q3, with AI spending, much of it on imported capital goods, accounting for over half of that growth. Another strong quarter is expected in Q4.
GS estimates AI-related hardware and IP spending will exceed $900bn annualized by end-2026 (+$550bn vs 2025) and reach $1.4tn by end-2027 (+$500bn), roughly 4% of US GDP.

AI investment is estimated to add 5.3pp to 2027 true capex growth but 4.3pp to measured capex growth, and 0.6pp to true GDP growth but 0.2pp to measured GDP growth. GS forecasts 2027 real business fixed investment growth of 8% Q4/Q4 vs consensus 4.2%, and 2027 real GDP growth of 2.4% Q4/Q4.

Midterm risk to AI investment is modest for now. GS expects newly elected Democratic governors in Texas, Georgia and Michigan, which hold over a third of planned US data centre capacity, to impose moratoria on new data centres. These should hit only unpermitted projects, leaving most 2027 construction unaffected. Stricter or longer moratoria are a downside risk mainly in 2028-2029.

GS Global Economics (Peters): core inflation mostly surprised to the downside in major economies after the start of the war in Iran, but US September and October inflation surprised to the upside. Global import and producer prices have risen and broadened.

Upstream price increases take 6-12 months on average to pass through to consumer prices, so residual pressure should continue into 1H 2027. Country team forecasts have been revised up (vs February 2026) through June 2027. Historical relationships imply 0.1-0.2pp cumulative upside to consensus inflation over the next 9 months, which could prompt modest further central bank tightening in early 2027.

Equities (Privorotsky): the 11 Nov rally was narrow and led by semis: SOX +5.5%, ARM +12%, MU +12%, while MSFT, META and AMZN closed lower. Retail Favorites (GSXURFAV) rose 495bps, its 3rd best day in three years, with three sub-$4 stocks accounting for 32% of US tape volume. NVDA fell roughly 9% overnight, weighing on Asia tech, and governance issues at Nvidia are forcing a significant rebalancing of capital.

Vol and positioning have largely reset: the SPX vol curve un-inverted, dealer skew flattened, and systematic L/S managers posted their best two-day return in nearly three years (+2.15%). Open question is whether the rally is mechanical short covering from low positioning or the start of something more durable. Breadth remains narrow.

AI hardware: GS separates compute demand from valuation multiples. Hyperscalers are best positioned given balance sheet capacity and contracted infrastructure. Four overhangs: higher cost of capital, power/permitting constraints, supply/demand balance entering 2028, and monetization velocity vs capex. Expects episodic, high-beta rallies rather than buy-and-hold, with strong micro results alongside multiple compression.

Risk view: may be only a bear market rally. A durable breakout probably needs lower rates, lower energy and broader leadership (hyperscalers, transportation, cyclicals, aerospace; defense looks washed out), but these struggle against an aggressive hiking cycle and high oil. Base case is chop rather than breakout, with low positioning and high vol as short-term tailwinds.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning has been reset materially, vol remains elevated, and the market keeps finding a bid while absorbing heavy Nvidia-specific pressure without broader capitulation. Low positioning and high vol are described as powerful short-term tailwinds.
tension_points.bear_case: The rally may be a bear market rally driven by short covering. Breadth is narrow, and a durable breakout needs lower rates, lower energy and broader leadership, which are hard to get against an aggressive hiking cycle and high oil.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Absent lower rates and lower energy prices, GS expects the market to chop rather than break out.

tension_points.bull_case: The view that inflation is ultimately a somewhat transitory process should not be abandoned, and noisy categories (airfares, health insurance, car prices) printed to the downside in October.
tension_points.bear_case: October CPI still printed 30bps, September and October US inflation surprised to the upside, and upstream price pressure should pass through into 1H 2027, adding 0.1-0.2pp of upside to consensus.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further upside surprises in US inflation data over the next 9 months would invalidate the transitory view and could prompt modest central bank tightening in early 2027.
